title: A European Public Investment Outlook
abstract: The essays in this outlook collectively foster a broad approach to and definition of public investment, that is today more relevant than ever. Offering up a timely and clear case for the elimination of bias against investment in European fiscal rules, this outlook is a welcome contribution to the European debate, aimed both at policy makers and general readers.

narrative:
Short impact summary

A European Public Investment Outlook shows strong scholarly and usage impact. The book has 54 citations in OpenAlex and sits in the top 1% of works for its field and year, while recorded usage is substantial, with 40,400 downloads across major open-access platforms. The evidence points to a book that has been taken up both in academic debate and by a wider readership interested in European public investment policy.

Full narrative

Published by Open Book Publishers in 2020, A European Public Investment Outlook by Floriana Cerniglia and Francesco Saraceno addresses public investment as a central issue in European fiscal and economic policy. Its impact record is led by scholarly uptake: the book has accumulated 54 OpenAlex citations and is positioned in the top 1% most-cited works for its field and publication year. That combination suggests the volume quickly became a reference point in ongoing discussions about public investment, fiscal rules, and European economic governance.

The citing landscape shows that the book’s influence is concentrated in policy-relevant and interdisciplinary areas. It is cited most often in work on fiscal policy and economic growth, regional development and policy, climate change policy and economics, and energy and environment. Citations appear across articles, book chapters, and books, indicating that the argument has circulated beyond a single niche and into broader conversations about growth, investment, and public policy.

Usage signals reinforce that this is an actively consulted book, not only a cited one. The record shows 40,400 downloads, with activity captured through Open Book Publishers, OAPEN, and Google Books. The book is also present in library holdings, which is consistent with adoption in research and teaching environments, although the available data do not provide direct course-listing evidence.

Open access has likely supported that reach: the book is available as diamond open access, with multiple repository instances recorded. Overall, the evidence portrays a book with clear academic influence, strong discoverability, and sustained reader interest, especially around the policy design of public investment in Europe.
